check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 errors).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 50 ul is below what the p1000_single_gen2 can measure (100 ul at
least)
   line 60:  p1000.aspirate(50, tubes[source_well_names[i]])
   At line 60 the p1000_single_gen2 is asked to draw 50 ul, below its minimum of 100 ul
   (this line did it 24 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the
   wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The
   simulator passes the move. Wells: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in
   slot 2.
   Affected: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [51709885806b]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: pbs (well A1 in slot 3)
   line 62:  p1000.aspirate(450, pbs_reservoir["A1"])
   At line 62 the tip went into pbs (well A1 in slot 3) while it still carried serum 1 (tube
   A1 in slot 2), serum 2 (tube A2 in slot 2), serum 3 (tube A3 in slot 2), serum 4 (tube A4
   in slot 2) and 20 more from an earlier step (this line did it 24 times). A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted
   material along into 69 other wells: wells A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in
   slot 4; wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 5.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Also reached 69 other wells: wells A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in slot 4;
   wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 38 more in slot 5.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 62 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [cd61a2264d6a]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
